findings.reason: the plan's own data says most hours are underfed, so the node needs a floor (a minimum number of fed hours, or a named measured window) or the head head of the section is never exercised.
findings.text: the fed-hour predicate ("less than 10% of its time below width to slots not taken") can be true of no hour in an eight-hour night, and the remaining requirement is only that each hour be listed with its attribution, so the section can be closed while never showing an hour that held 95% of plateau

findings.reason: a control that is merely recorded beside the result leaves the section's one measure unfalsified.
findings.text: the negative control is "the same reading over 17 November ... is logged beside it", a comparison that does not have to fail, so it cannot show that the 95%-of-plateau measure ever rejects

findings.reason: the published quantity is the endpoint §7 and the dispatchers consume; left ambiguous, the repair can overshoot the lane instead of sizing it.
findings.text: §4 defines "capacity" as margin × width ÷ offered load but never states which published field carries it, while the `worker_slots` field it names publishes spare slots ("how many more workers the router would admit now", `imas_ambix/agent/router.py`, `llm_watch` band), so a node can publish a total worker target into a field every dispatcher reads as headroom

findings.reason: the two sections that the followup starts first depend on an input that does not exist in the tree, so the nodes must either hunt outside the repository or write tests against aggregates that are not the receipts the calibration describes.
findings.text: §3's test calibrates "from a committed excerpt of receipts covering 18 November 04:45 to 06:40 UTC" and §6 cross-checks "the committed receipt excerpts", but no such excerpt is committed anywhere in the repository (`git ls-files` and a filesystem search find only the derived calibration/log files), and the plan names no source for it

findings.reason: the analytic settle (margin × width ÷ offered load) is recoverable from §4 itself, so a worker can compute the band; this is a clarity gap rather than a wrong path.
findings.text: §4's simulation arm holds the worker count "within 15% of its settled value" without defining the settled value or the window over which it is measured, so the 15% band has no computable reference
